M1: The Crab Nebula from Hubble

This is the mess that is left when a star explodes. The Crab Nebula, the result of a supernova seen in 1054 AD, is filled with mysterious filaments. The filaments are not only tremendously complex, but appear to have less mass than expelled in the original supernova and a higher speed than expected from a free explosion. This image, taken by the Hubble Space Telescope, is presented in three colors chosen for scientific interest. The Crab Nebula spans about 10 light-years. In the nebula's very center lies a pulsar: a neutron star as massive as the Sun but with only the size of a small town. The Crab Pulsar rotates about 30 times each second.

Are You a Thinking Thing? Why Debating Machine Consciousness Matters

Very very interesting re: Ray Kurzweil, and his recent thoughts on spirituality and God -- it's here, about 7 minutes, if you want to view it too. But I really think it's mind-boggling important, because it touches on the next wave of consciousness.

There is the first wave -- the completely unconscious level. Stones, volcanoes, etc. Then there are worms and animals all the way up to the primate level -- kind of semi-conscious -- which have some level of awareness, but not human. Then of course there is the human level -- and the next wave is God. We are about to go to the next level -- the God-like level -- in thirty or forty years, within our lifetime.

I believe that's what he really means, and I essentially think so too. This is at the core of his monumental breakthrough to AI, and I think it's right on.

I studied artificial intelligence, and no one will ever be able to convince me that any machine or program will have a silicon soul. Elon Musk, Stephen Hawking, and whatever other supposedly intelligent famous person seriously do not know what they are talking about. With that being said, giving machines the ability to kill without human intervention is dangerous simply because software sucks - not because they'll take over the world. A machine will never transcend its programming. Robotics engineers may make robots that seem creepily similar to humans, but they are nothing but toasters just using cries to indicate something wrong versus a blinking light. Machine consciousness is not science fiction; it is fantasy.
